findings.Quote: He went where she kept the people who weren't lying and weren't helping — the largest group there was.
findings.Note: Aphoristic filler that generalizes past the scene rather than showing Yemina's specific read on Achebe; reads as authorial commentary.
findings.Fix: Cut or ground it in a concrete observation about Achebe specifically.

findings.Quote: The room told her what every room told her, if she paid attention
findings.Note: Aphoristic framing that tells us Yemina's method as universal wisdom rather than showing it in the specific moment; feels like authorial commentary intruding on the scene.
findings.Fix: Cut the generalization; let the categories list follow directly from the room without the framing sentence.

findings.Quote: a shape nobody else believed in
findings.Fix: replace vague 'shape' abstraction with a concrete image of what she'd been chasing

findings.Quote: The weight would not leave her chest, and by it she understood that what she was doing was not confirmation. It was closer to grief.
findings.Note: Tells the emotion directly rather than letting the empty search result and her subsequent restraint (not running it again) carry the grief, undercutting the 'felt loss' the beat is meant to earn through action.
findings.Fix: Cut the naming of 'grief' and let the physical detail (cold tea, thumb on the key, not running it again) stand alone as the evidence of feeling.

findings.Quote: tasted like chocolate described to someone who'd never eaten food
findings.Note: Clever-sounding simile that doesn't survive literal scrutiny — a flavor description relayed secondhand to a person with no reference for food is a nonsensical mechanism for producing a taste at all.
findings.Fix: Ground it in a real flavor failure: 'tasted like chocolate flavoring with the chocolate left out.'

findings.Quote: like teeth in a receded gum
findings.Note: Worn simile for exposed/pitted surfaces, undercuts the otherwise precise material observation.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific, non-anatomical comparison rooted in the concrete's own material logic.

findings.Quote: the way skin looks where a wound has scarred but not settled
findings.Note: Second body-based simile in the same passage (echoing the teeth/gum image just above) — repetition of anatomical comparison weakens the device rather than reinforcing it.
findings.Fix: Vary the register; use a construction-material or weather-based comparison instead to avoid doubling up on body imagery.

findings.Quote: Fifteen years had taught her that the doors that hurt worst were the ones held shut by people certain they were doing their jobs.
findings.Note: Pseudo-profound aphorism delivering the theme directly rather than dramatizing it — tells the reader the point of the beat instead of letting Achebe's behavior make it.
findings.Fix: Trim to action/observation, let the door-blocking gesture carry the meaning without the summary line.

findings.Quote: the largest group there was
findings.Note: Undercuts the specific bureaucratic-closure point (the purpose) by generalizing Achebe into 'most people,' diluting the institutional critique into a broader cynicism about humanity.
findings.Fix: Remove the universalizing tail so the observation stays targeted at institutional behavior.

findings.Quote: the way a coat holds the shape of the body that took it off
findings.Note: Purple simile that strains under literal scrutiny — a coat holds a body's shape while worn, not as a record of departure; the comparison doesn't quite track logically.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more literal image of absence, e.g. dust outlines or worn desk edges.

findings.Quote: a face that fell open the way some faces fall into suspicion
findings.Note: Vague, almost-meaningless descriptive turn — 'falls open' as contrasted with 'falls into suspicion' doesn't clarify what his face actually communicates.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete facial detail.

findings.Quote: The classroom held its quiet like a held breath.
findings.Note: Stock personification/cliché pairing quiet with held breath, slightly undercutting the otherwise sharp sensory writing around it.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile; the drone/echo detail already establishes the quiet.

findings.Quote: she held it steady the way you hold a hand steady over a cut you don't want a child to be frightened by
findings.Note: Overextended simile that tells the reader Yemina is being protective/composed rather than showing it through concrete behavior; slightly purple relative to the plain prose around it.
findings.Fix: Shorten to a plainer action, e.g. 'she kept it flat.'

findings.Quote: A man who's filed a report says yes in about a second, because the report is a thing he did, an object that exists, and remembering it costs him nothing.
findings.Note: Slightly over-explained aphoristic reasoning that tells us how to interpret timing rather than trusting the scene.
findings.Fix: Trim to the core observation without the explanatory clause about cost.

findings.Quote: the way a bright thing does
findings.Note: Vague filler simile that doesn't add specific sensory content.
findings.Fix: Cut the comparison or make it concrete (e.g., 'the way a screen does after you look away').

findings.Quote: You don't spend six weeks bringing a child to a frequency in order to make her disappear. Disappearing takes no tuning at all; the city does it to people for free, by the thousand, and never leaves a print to mark the spot.
findings.Note: Reads as a pseudo-profound aphorism about the city that briefly shifts from character reasoning to universal-truth commentary.
findings.Fix: Tighten to the investigative logic without the generalized editorializing about the city.

findings.Quote: the way a photograph of someone's idea of a kind face doesn't age into kindness
findings.Note: Convoluted meta-simile that requires unpacking and strains under literal scrutiny (a photograph doesn't 'age into' anything by nature).
findings.Fix: Simplify to a more direct image of dated, uncanny warmth.

findings.Quote: She felt the wrongness before she understood it, the way a foot feels a stair that isn't where it expected one.
findings.Note: Serviceable but slightly stock sensory analogy; sits close to cliché territory for 'wrongness' beats.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile or replace with something more specific to her neuretics experience.

findings.Quote: the way you get certain of a forged signature — not from one stroke but from all of them being, quietly, not yours
findings.Note: The 'not yours' twist on a forged signature is a slightly labored construction that draws attention to its own cleverness rather than the sensation.
findings.Fix: Simplify to something less rhetorically symmetrical, e.g. 'the way you recognize a forged signature — every stroke slightly wrong, none of them wrong enough to name.'

findings.Quote: the way a fire investigator looks at the burn spread before the door
findings.Note: Slightly ornamental analogy that isn't earned elsewhere in her characterization; reads as inserted color rather than her actual method.
findings.Fix: Cut or ground it in her own established investigative habits instead of a borrowed profession.

findings.Quote: She'd been handed his file at 10:14 the morning before, four hours before the case existed, from a sender field that wasn't redacted, just empty.
findings.Note: This detail is dropped in abruptly without connecting to the forty-seven pattern the beat is meant to deliver; it gestures at a new revelation (pre-knowledge of Bramley specifically) that dilutes the systemic-scale payoff the beat promises.
findings.Fix: Either integrate this as part of the pattern's implication or move/expand it so it doesn't read as a stray addendum.

findings.Quote: It was built to make them the same size, so that no single desk would ever have to hold one and feel that it weighed more than the other.
findings.Note: Borders on aphoristic overstatement about bureaucracy's intent — reads as authorial commentary rather than Yemina's grounded observation.
findings.Fix: Trim to a more concrete observation, e.g. 'The form didn't distinguish. That was its whole design.'

findings.Quote: one careful person letting another keep her hands free for the work
findings.Note: Slightly precious phrasing that tips into sentimentality for a beat meant to establish procedural, understated detail.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory clause and let the silence stand without naming its meaning.

findings.Quote: the gesture of a man placing a document into a record, except there was no record here, only her. So he'd made her the record.
findings.Note: Overworked, slightly redundant explanation of the gesture's meaning — tells the reader the metaphor's point twice.
findings.Fix: Trim to one clause, e.g. 'the gesture of a man filing evidence — except the only record here was her.'

findings.Quote: the kind of stillness that can look like shock from outside
findings.Note: Generic description of grief-stillness that reads as a stock qualifier rather than a specific observation.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete physical detail unique to Abena.

findings.Quote: a theory is a thing you build for the form to receive, and the form receives it last
findings.Note: Aphoristic, slightly opaque maxim that reads as authorial wisdom rather than Yemina's lived method; slows the methodological setup the beat needs to establish cleanly.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete procedural statement of what she does instead of theorizing.

findings.Quote: a small administrative fact clipped to a child like a coat-check tag
findings.Note: The simile strains — coat-check tags are for retrieving property, an odd/uncomfortable comparison to a child's medical flag that reads as reaching for cleverness rather than precision.
findings.Fix: Use a plainer comparison or drop the simile.

findings.Quote: a thing on you that isn't yours
findings.Note: Slightly redundant restatement of 'borrowed coat' that adds little beyond the preceding clause.
findings.Fix: Cut the trailing clause; the coat image already carries the meaning.

findings.Quote: the way a school android smiles at a question it's been told not to answer
findings.Note: Ornamental simile that introduces a new image (school android) not otherwise present in the story's texture, feels imported for flavor rather than precision.
findings.Fix: Replace with a simpler description of the system's non-committal flag.

findings.Quote: which Yemina noticed the way she noticed everything: a person who has decided what she doesn't know is as deliberate as a person who has decided what she does
findings.Fix: cut the aphoristic doubling; state the observation once, plainly

findings.Quote: Yemina turned the phrase over the way she turned over a clause in a contract, looking for the place it had been written to hide
findings.Fix: trim the simile; it explains her professional habit rather than showing new insight

findings.Quote: and they both heard which of the two it was
findings.Fix: cut; redundant restatement of the preceding sentence's point

findings.Quote: Not a city waking up — a machine that never stopped, only changed gears.
findings.Note: Stock negation-construction opener ('not X, but Y') doing abstract table-setting rather than concrete image work; reads as scene-setting shorthand rather than earned observation.
findings.Fix: Cut the abstraction and let the concrete details (the train, the shift change) establish the machine-like rhythm without naming it.

findings.Quote: The seam ran straight down the centerline of a bridge that didn't know it had been split in two.
findings.Note: Personifying the bridge ('didn't know') is a soft anthropomorphic tic that slightly undercuts the otherwise rigorous bureaucratic-logic voice of the passage.
findings.Fix: State the split as administrative fact without granting the bridge awareness, e.g. 'a bridge split by paperwork no engineer had ever been told about.'

findings.Quote: in the flat institutional font that never meant anything good
findings.Note: Vague genre-filler aside — 'never meant anything good' is a stock aphoristic tag rather than a specific observation.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause or replace with a concrete visual detail of the banner.

findings.Quote: Arguing was something you did to a person, and there was no person here — only the architecture, doing what it was built to do
findings.Note: Borderline pseudo-profound aphorism explaining Yemina's restraint rather than dramatizing it; slightly on-the-nose thesis statement for the beat's institutional-obstruction point.
findings.Fix: Compress to action: she pockets the credential without protest, let the notebook line carry the meaning.

findings.Quote: she looked at the blank the way she'd looked at Kito's empty chair
findings.Fix: replace with a more specific, less symmetrical comparison or cut the simile

findings.Quote: Silence was not an answer. She'd learned that fifteen years ago and relearned it every year since, and it still cost her something each time.
findings.Fix: cut the generalized aphorism; let the silence itself carry the weight without the summary statement

findings.Quote: An open case wasn't a door. It was a status.
findings.Fix: cut or fold into action; the metaphor-then-correction pattern reads as a rhetorical device rather than earned realization

findings.Quote: The lake cold found it the way it found everything in the Veil — sideways, coming up from the south where the buildings opened.
findings.Note: Reads as atmospheric filler that doesn't clarify anything about the geography and leans on personification that doesn't quite hold literally (cold 'finding' things sideways).
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete sensory detail specific to this yard.

findings.Quote: bright and patient
findings.Note: Personifying the playground colors as 'patient' is a soft, vague emotional projection rather than concrete observation, slightly undercutting the otherwise sharp forensic tone.
findings.Fix: Replace with a harder, more clinical description, e.g. 'bright, unweathered, wrong.'

findings.Quote: Yemina watched the change happen — the way you watch a temperature drop on a gauge instead of feeling it on your skin.
findings.Note: A slightly labored simile that tells us she's detached rather than showing the change itself with more specificity.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile and let the described physical change (stopping laughing, door-closing beat) carry the meaning.

findings.Quote: the way a door closes when someone on the far side decides it should
findings.Note: A worn figurative construction for sudden emotional shutdown.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific physical beat unique to Bear.

findings.Quote: the way you hold a thing handed to you at a funeral
findings.Note: A generic, slightly sentimental comparison that tells us the emotional register instead of letting the specific physical description (chest height, two hands, unbroken seal) do the work.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile; the preceding and following details already convey the gravity.

findings.Quote: She had a word for what she'd have felt, standing where he stood, holding what he held. Watching him, she couldn't make the word fit.
findings.Note: Vague gesture at unnamed emotion without content; reads as a placeholder for insight rather than actual observation.
findings.Fix: Either name the word and explain the mismatch concretely, or cut.

findings.Quote: carrying whatever the four minutes had cost him somewhere she couldn't see and wouldn't be shown
findings.Fix: Cut the metaphor abstraction; state plainly what she observed (his continued laughter, nothing visibly changed) without the poetic 'carrying' figure.

findings.Quote: She had built her whole method on finishing what she started. She wasn't going to stop finis
findings.Note: Sentence cuts off mid-word, and the line itself reads as a stated-not-shown character summary rather than earned characterization.
findings.Fix: Complete the sentence and consider showing this through the paperwork itself rather than asserting the method.
